text.p: Coffee prices were boosted on Friday as buying from roasters and speculators was prompted by a port workers strike at major South American exporter.
But most other commodities moved fairly narrowly apart from zinc prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME).
Coffee traders said that buyers appeared to have decided that now was the time to build up positions in anticipation of possible supply bottlenecks.
Still low stocks in North America along with speculation that the Brazilian crop may be at the lower end of expectations have been underpinning prices recently.
But this week's strike by workers at Buenaventura, the port which handles 60 percent of the coffee exported by the world's number two producer Colombia gave prices an additional boost.
"U.S. roasters are crying out for coffee because we understand their stocks are running low. But for the time being there is nothing we can do," Colombian coffee official John Naranjo said.
In London LIFFE coffee futures rose around $20 with the March position trading up to $1,350 a tonne.

Speculators were attracted to the LME zinc contract where prices had at long last broken out of a near two year trading range. The three months delivery price reached $1,147 a tonne, its highest level for 23 months.
